source.version: Journal version of record, Frontiers in Psychology 17:1847432, published 17 June 2026 (p. 1).
source.title_on_document: Effects of integrating a structured design thinking strategy into generative AI-supported design learning on students’ design achievement, creative self-efficacy, and problem-solving skills

supplement.holds: Supplementary Table S1 contains the Double Diamond-Based Design Operation Sheet (p. 5, section 3.3). Supplement not included or examined; no statistics are identified as available only there.

paper_design_summary: In a university character-design course in China, 120 animation undergraduates were individually randomly assigned to structured design thinking plus GAI, GAI alone, or traditional design learning (p. 4, sections 3.1-3.2). Students worked independently using Deepseek and Dreamina in the AI conditions, or conventional design resources and software in the control (pp. 4-7, section 3.3). Instructors scored final artwork using a rubric including creativity; other endpoints were self-reported creative self-efficacy and problem-solving ability (pp. 8-9, sections 3.4-3.5).

assignment.what_was_assigned: Three of six existing classes were sampled, then individual students were randomly assigned to GAI-SDTS, GAI, or TDL and reorganized into mixed-class groups (p. 4, section 3.2). The authors call the design quasi-experimental despite explicitly describing individual random assignment.
assignment.quote: All students in the selected classes were then randomly assigned to one of three groups:

arms.name: GAI-SDTS
arms.description: Deepseek and Dreamina with a Double Diamond-Based Design Operation Sheet and GAI operational training (pp. 4-8, sections 3.2-3.5). Initial N = 40 in Figure 8 and analyzed N = 40 in Table 1 (p. 9).

arms.name: GAI
arms.description: Free use of the same Deepseek and Dreamina tools and operational training, without structured design thinking guidance (pp. 5 and 8-9). Initial N = 40 in Figure 8 and analyzed N = 40 in Table 1 (p. 9).

arms.name: TDL
arms.description: Traditional Design Learning using printed/online references, hand-drawn sketches, and conventional software such as Photoshop, without GAI or explicit design thinking (pp. 4-5). Initial N = 40 in Figure 8 and analyzed N = 40 in Table 1 (p. 9).

participants.exclusions: No exclusions or attrition are reported. Methods describe random assignment of all selected students; Figure 8 shows 40 per condition before pre-questionnaires, and Table 1 analyzes 40 per condition. Intention-to-treat analysis is not explicitly claimed.
participants.who: Second-year undergraduate animation majors at one university in central China.
participants.locator: p. 4, section 3.2; p. 9, Figure 8 and Table 1.

ai_tool.name_model: Deepseek and Dreamina; model versions not stated.
ai_tool.how_used: Deepseek supported open text dialogue, ideation, character concepts, prompts, and design statements. Dreamina supported text-to-image and image-to-image generation, variation, refinement, and final export. Structured use in GAI-SDTS and free use in GAI (pp. 5-7, section 3.3). Open chat and refinement were additional roles.

task.description: Independently create a distinctive card-game character with clear personality traits, through exploration, definition, creation, and presentation (p. 4, sections 3.2-3.3). Final artwork was graded (p. 9, section 3.5).
task.duration: Four-week practical course, October 20 to November 14, 2025 (p. 4, section 3.2). The procedure places training in Week 1, design work in Weeks 2-5, and grading in Week 6; Figure 8 shows 90 minutes/week of design work and 90 minutes of AI training (pp. 8-9, section 3.5 and Figure 8).

outcomes.name: Design achievement: composite expert rating of final artwork
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two instructors with 8 years of design-teaching experience independently rated anonymized, randomly ordered final artwork. Rubric dimensions: Technical Skill; Adherence to Theme; Composition and Design; Creativity; Detail Quality and Workload. Each is rated from 1 to 5; Kendall’s W = 0.94, p < 0.001 (p. 8, section 3.4). Only the combined design-achievement score is reported; separate dimension results and exact aggregation across dimensions/raters are not supplied. Coded as usefulness because it measures broad artwork quality including creativity. A one-way ANOVA analyzes students’ design-achievement scores (p. 9, sections 4-4.1 and Table 1).
outcomes.delay: Course-end grading in Week 6 of artwork produced during Weeks 2-5, with AI available in AI arms (p. 9, section 3.5). No separate delayed production task. Authors explicitly acknowledge that AI generated and refined the rated outputs (p. 11, section 5.1).

contrasts.reported: GAI: M = 18.65, SD = 7.41, N = 40; TDL: M = 16.13, SD = 6.85, N = 40. Tukey HSD: GAI > TDL, p < 0.001. Three-group omnibus ANOVA: F = 43.28, p < 0.001 (not a pairwise test).
GAI-SDTS: M = 20.90, SD = 7.64, N = 40; TDL: M = 16.13, SD = 6.85, N = 40. Tukey HSD: GAI-SDTS > TDL, p < 0.001. Three-group omnibus ANOVA: F = 43.28, p < 0.001 (not a pairwise test).
GAI-SDTS: M = 20.90, SD = 7.64, N = 40; GAI: M = 18.65, SD = 7.41, N = 40. Tukey HSD: GAI-SDTS > GAI, p < 0.001. Three-group omnibus ANOVA: F = 43.28, p < 0.001 (not a pairwise test).

company_involvement.description: No company involvement reported; authors are affiliated with Universiti Sains Malaysia. No financial support or commercial/financial relationships are declared.
company_involvement.locator: p. 1, affiliation; p. 14, Funding and Conflict of interest.

eligibility.reason: Individual random assignment to GAI conditions or conventional non-AI coursework is explicit, despite the quasi-experimental label (pp. 3-4, sections 3.1-3.2). There are 120 analyzed students, 40 per arm (p. 4, section 3.2; p. 9, Table 1). Instructors score final creative artwork using a rubric explicitly including Creativity and design quality (p. 8, section 3.4). AI helped produce the graded artwork, supporting with_ai (pp. 7-9, sections 3.3-3.5; p. 11, section 5.1). Eligibility rests on the output rubric, not self-reports; results are for the broad composite, with no separate creativity estimate.

one_line_finding: Among 120 students, mean design-achievement scores were 20.90 with structured design thinking plus GAI, 18.65 with GAI alone, and 16.13 with traditional learning; all Tukey pairwise p < 0.001 are reported (p. 4, section 3.2; p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1).
open_questions: Table 1 means, SDs, and group sizes appear inconsistent with the reported F = 43.28 and all Tukey pairwise p < 0.001; verify against underlying data before effect-size extraction. Printed values are retained unchanged (p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1).
How were rubric dimensions and instructor ratings aggregated, and are separate Creativity-dimension results available? Only the combined score is reported (p. 8, section 3.4; p. 9, Table 1).
Randomization implementation is not specified, and the authors use a quasi-experimental label despite explicit individual random assignment (pp. 3-4, sections 3.1-3.2).
notes: Entire markdown read, including references; no appendix or supplement is included in the 16-page PDF. Checked PDF text for methods, counts, instruments, results, and disclosures; recovered Table 1 with find_tables and visually checked Figure 8/Table 1 in memory. One reported output endpoint is coded: the design-achievement composite, with its component criteria preserved in measure_detail. Separate component analyses are absent. Creative self-efficacy and perceived problem-solving scores/subscales are excluded because they are self-reports (p. 8, section 3.4). No diversity or independent after-AI output is reported. TDL is coded as conventional coursework (ai_vs_bau), including ordinary references and Photoshop (p. 5). Contrasts use the same sample and share comparison arms. No reanalysis or sample overlap is identified; Bian et al. (2025) supplies the rubric, not evidence of shared participants (p. 8). No data/code URL is given; authors promise raw data availability (p. 14). No effect sizes or standard errors were calculated.
